subject: Actionable model-fit plan + request for customer prompt samples
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@novaprospect.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up + next steps from today's demo

Alex / Sana — thanks again for taking time this morning. High-level recap from our side and clear next steps so we stay action-oriented:

• Goal alignment: NovaProspect is prioritizing accurate, low-latency extraction of candidate summaries and automated QA for recruiter notes (80% of queries are <= 200 tokens).
• Success metrics you called out: 92% extraction precision on entity sets, median latency < 120ms at 1x traffic, and clear regression monitoring for hallucination events.
• Top risk: presence of PII in sample prompts (SSNs, candidate emails) — you asked how we handle redaction in intake.

Concrete next steps I committed to:
1) Share a pragmatic model-fit recommendation and benchmark links tailored to a 200-token distribution.
2) Send a simple prompt-sample template you can use to export 30–50 real user prompts (including a column to flag sensitive fields).
3) Outline redaction guidance and a lightweight intake checklist so your legal/safety team can sign off quickly.

I'm attaching a one-page prompt_samples_template.csv to make it as easy as possible for your team. If you can populate even 20 representative prompts (including the edge cases you mentioned — abbreviations, mixed-language names, and truncated resumes), we can run a quick intake eval and come back with a focused benchmark within 3 business days.

Recommended models (preliminary):
- For best cost/latency trade-off: opt-2-13b quantized (recommended config: int8, sequence cap 256).
- For highest fidelity on edge-case extraction: Llama2-70b-v2 (dedicated pool, can be used for canary comparisons).

I'll follow up with the intake checklist and a short Drive folder for uploads. If you prefer, we can accept an SFTP drop or a shared dataset via your secure portal.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182
Redwood Inference

Attachment: prompt_samples_template.csv (CSV schema: prompt_text, source_type, expected_output, contains_pii [yes/no], pii_fields_description, notes)

From: Alex Morgan <alex@novaprospect.com>

Cc: Sana Iqbal <sana@novaprospect.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Oct 2028 11:03:00 -0700

Marissa — helpful summary, thanks. A couple quick clarifications: 

1) We'll prioritize recruiter note extraction; I can pull a CSV export with 25 sample prompts and flag PII. Expect that by end-of-day Friday.
2) For performance: our internal SLA is 100ms median at peak. Curious whether the opt-2 suggestion hits that if we run continuous batching, or whether we should aim for a smaller family on dedicated capacity.
3) Redaction: legal wants to see the intake checklist before we ship samples. Can you share the checklist and the small redaction primer you mentioned?

Also looping in Sana (head of data ops) on logistics.

—Alex
Director of Product, NovaProspect
alex@novaprospect.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@novaprospect.com>, Sana Iqbal <sana@novaprospect.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Oct 2028 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Model-fit plan, intake checklist, and benchmark links (attachments)

Alex / Sana — attached is a short intake checklist and a redaction primer that your legal/safety folks can scan quickly. TL;DR version and action items below. Full docs are in the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AaBbCcExample

What we propose for the quick intake eval (scope = 20–30 prompts you provide):
1) Run those prompts across 3 candidate serving configs:
   • opt-2-13b (int8, streaming enabled) — target median latency 85–140ms depending on traffic/batching.
   • llama2-70b-v2 (fp16, dedicated pool) — used as fidelity guardrail for hallucination-sensitive prompts.
   • a small LLM family (7b quantized) if you want an ultra-low-cost baseline for A/B tests.
2) We'll return a short report with: precision/recall on entity extraction, hallucination flags, latency P50/P95 at your profile, and a short cost-per-100k-token estimate.

Redaction & PII intake guidance (summary):
• Please mark samples with contains_pii=yes where applicable. For those rows, replace PII with <REDACTED:TYPE> where TYPE is email/ssn/phone/name.
• If you can provide a second column with the unredacted field mapping in a password-protected file (or a secure SFTP drop), we can use that for internal labeling only and then delete per your retention policy.
• For edge cases (e.g., initials only, merged name/title lines, non-latin characters), flag with notes so our eval focuses on those.

Benchmark links (examples we've used to validate similar recruiters workflows):
• https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/opt-2-quantized-vs-llama2 (includes sample scripts and runner config)

Attachments included: nova_eval_benchmark_results.pdf (example report), prompt_samples_template.csv (same as earlier).

If you can drop samples by EOD Friday, we'll prioritize an intake run Monday and aim to deliver the short report by Wednesday. If legal needs to review the redaction primer first, tell me and we'll delay sample use until you confirm.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182

Quick internal note — loop for next steps: 

1) Once NovaProspect drops the CSV, Karthik, can you schedule the intake eval on our sandbox cluster (opt-2-13b int8) and tag the run NP-2028-021? Use the small-run config (max batch 16) to reflect their latency needs.
2) I'll prepare a one-page brief for their legal summarizing our redaction controls and retention policy (to attach to the Drive folder).
3) If their median target is 100ms strict, flag to Marissa that we may need dedicated capacity for canary testing on the 7b/13b family — otherwise the continuous-batching tradeoff will push P50 above target under load.

Assigning owners: Karthik -> intake run scheduling; Ben -> legal brief; Marissa -> follow and confirm SLA preference with the customer.

Ben
